tagline: What everyone's streaming, the films worth seeing, and Hong Kong cinema's comeback.
why: 'Watched anything good lately?' is the safest question in small talk. Streaming has turned TV into a global water-cooler, with Korean, Japanese and Hong Kong shows competing with Hollywood. Knowing the big franchises, the prestige series, the directors people admire and what's trending lets you recommend, react and swap opinions easily.

essentials.title: Streaming rules
essentials.body: Netflix is the giant, followed by Disney+, Apple TV, Amazon Prime Video and HBO Max. Viu and local platforms carry Asian shows.

essentials.title: Prestige TV
essentials.body: Big-budget, critically loved series like Succession, The Last of Us, Severance and The White Lotus drive conversation.

essentials.title: Franchises dominate cinemas
essentials.body: Marvel, Star Wars, Fast & Furious and animated hits fill multiplexes, though superhero fatigue is a real debate.

essentials.title: Asian content goes global
essentials.body: Squid Game, Parasite and anime like Demon Slayer showed non-English stories can be global hits.

essentials.title: Awards season
essentials.body: The Oscars (March), Golden Globes and Emmys spark debate. Hong Kong has its own Hong Kong Film Awards in April.

essentials.title: Directors as brands
essentials.body: Christopher Nolan, Denis Villeneuve, Bong Joon-ho, Greta Gerwig and Wong Kar-wai have devoted fans.

names.name: Christopher Nolan
names.what: Director of Inception, The Dark Knight and Oppenheimer (Best Picture 2024).

names.name: Bong Joon-ho
names.what: Director of Parasite, the first non-English Best Picture winner (2020).

names.name: Wong Kar-wai
names.what: Hong Kong auteur of In the Mood for Love and Chungking Express; made the TV series Blossoms Shanghai.

names.name: Squid Game
names.what: Korean Netflix series, the platform's most-watched show; its final season came out in 2025.

names.name: Stranger Things
names.what: Netflix's 1980s sci-fi hit, whose final season arrived in late 2025.

names.name: The White Lotus
names.what: HBO satire set in luxury resorts; season 3 was set in Thailand.

names.name: Ne Zha 2
names.what: Chinese animated film that became the highest-grossing animated film ever in 2025.

names.name: Stephen Chow
names.what: Hong Kong comedy legend behind Kung Fu Hustle and Shaolin Soccer.

names.name: Tony Leung Chiu-wai
names.what: Hong Kong's most acclaimed actor, star of Wong Kar-wai films and Marvel's Shang-Chi.

names.name: Andy Lau
names.what: Hong Kong superstar actor and singer.

names.name: Studio Ghibli / Hayao Miyazaki
names.what: Japanese animation studio behind Spirited Away; Oscar for The Boy and the Heron (2024).

names.name: Marvel Studios
names.what: The superhero franchise, trying to regain its 2019 Avengers: Endgame peak.

names.name: A24
names.what: Indie studio behind Everything Everywhere All at Once, starring Michelle Yeoh.

names.name: Michelle Yeoh
names.what: Malaysian star who started in Hong Kong action films and won the Best Actress Oscar in 2023.

timeline.event: Bruce Lee makes Hong Kong action cinema global.
Golden age of Hong Kong cinema: John Woo, Jackie Chan, Stephen Chow.
Titanic becomes the biggest film ever.
Infernal Affairs, later remade as The Departed.
Avengers: Endgame; Parasite wins the Palme d'Or.
Squid Game becomes a global phenomenon.
Barbenheimer; Everything Everywhere All at Once sweeps the Oscars.
Twilight of the Warriors: Walled In and The Last Dance break Hong Kong box office records for local films.
Ne Zha 2 earns over US$2 billion; Netflix's KPop Demon Hunters becomes its most-watched film.

now.headline: Godzilla Minus Zero tops the box office
now.detail: The Toho sequel opened at No. 1 in the US with US$30.6 million on 6-8 November, ahead of The Cat in the Hat.

now.headline: Hunger Games next
now.detail: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping opens 20 November, tracking for a US$50-70 million start.

now.headline: Big December showdown
now.detail: Avengers: Doomsday and Dune: Part Three both open on 18 December.

now.headline: Spider-Man rules 2026
now.detail: Spider-Man: Brand New Day is the year's top film in the US with about US$958 million, ahead of The Odyssey.

now.headline: On Netflix
now.detail: The One About Matthew Perry leads the series chart, and Keira Knightley's Black Doves is back for season 2.

local.headline: Hong Kong cinema revival
local.detail: Walled In, The Last Dance and The Prosecutor drew big local crowds, sparking talk of a comeback.

local.headline: TVB nostalgia
local.detail: TVB dramas defined Hong Kong TV for decades; people love reminiscing about classic series.

local.headline: Where to watch
local.detail: Cinemas like K11 Art House and Broadway Cinematheque; Netflix and Disney+ at home.

debates.question: Is the Marvel era over?
debates.sides: Recent films disappointed many, but big team-ups still draw crowds.

debates.question: Cinema or streaming?
debates.sides: The big screen experience vs convenience and price.

debates.question: Is Hong Kong cinema really back?
debates.sides: Strong hits vs a smaller industry than its golden age.

debates.question: Dubbed or subtitled?
debates.sides: Subtitles preserve performances; dubbing is easier.
